articles.body: Scalable API Architecture Insights with GraphQL The relentless chaos of hitting a daily API limit is the founder's curse. The intricacies of building efficient, scalable API architectures are often overshadowed by the harsh reality of technical debt and never-ending server tweaks. Here's the brutal truth: many tech solopreneurs are drowning in a sea of legacy REST APIs, struggling to keep up with modern requirements. Let me be clear, if you're not thinking about how GraphQL can improve your API strategy, you're already behind. The Core Technical Problem & Why This Matters The central challenge for any API architect lies in creating a balance between performance , scalability , and usability .
articles.author: Kevin Jang

articles.title: End-to-end tests that read real email, without a disposable-inbox service
articles.excerpt: By Jonas Birmé, Eyevinn Technology Our signup flow mails you a six digit login code. That one design choice makes end-to-end testing awkward, because a browser automation suite cannot sign up for anyt…
articles.body: By Jonas Birmé, Eyevinn Technology Our signup flow mails you a six digit login code. That one design choice makes end-to-end testing awkward, because a browser automation suite cannot sign up for anything unless it can read a real inbox. Playwright will happily fill the email field. The code arrives somewhere else entirely. The usual answer is a disposable-inbox API. You call an endpoint, you get a throwaway address, you poll for the message. We ran on one for about two years and it worked. But it was a second vendor, a second API key in CI, and a second thing that can be down while your tests go red for reasons that have nothing to do with your code. Then it occurred to us that we were already paying for a mailbox.
articles.author: Jonas Birmé

articles.title: Building AegisMesh: Autonomous Security Operations & Zero-Trust Mesh for Linux in Python 🛡️⚡
articles.excerpt: In modern cloud-native and distributed Linux environments, static perimeter defense is no longer enough. Infrastructure teams need continuous, automated visibility into running sockets, container priv…
articles.body: In modern cloud-native and distributed Linux environments, static perimeter defense is no longer enough. Infrastructure teams need continuous, automated visibility into running sockets, container privilege escalations, and zero-trust policy enforcement directly on the host. To solve this, I built AegisMesh — an open-source, autonomous Security Operations and Zero-Trust Mesh Platform engineered for Linux infrastructure. 🛡️ Why AegisMesh? Traditional security audits often happen after an incident or via heavy, expensive enterprise agents. AegisMesh is designed to be lightweight, autonomous, and developer-friendly, giving SREs and security engineers instant visibility into host vulnerabilities and runtime threats.

articles.title: Street Fighter 6 Data Fetch Issue: Automating Session ID Updates to Eliminate Manual URL Adjustments
articles.excerpt: Introduction The Street Fighter 6 website presents a unique challenge for developers attempting to automate data fetching: its session identifier, a critical component for accessing dynamic data, expi…
articles.body: Introduction The Street Fighter 6 website presents a unique challenge for developers attempting to automate data fetching: its session identifier , a critical component for accessing dynamic data, expires periodically and requires manual intervention to update fetch URLs. This issue is particularly frustrating for projects like browser extensions that aim to streamline data retrieval, such as counting "Legends" (top-rated players) for each character. The root of the problem lies in the opaque nature of session management on the website, which likely employs server-side handling of session identifiers, making them inaccessible through standard client-side mechanisms.

articles.title: Rust-Powered Developer Tooling: Why Modern Package Managers and Data Frameworks are Moving to Rust
articles.excerpt: Originally published on tamiz.pro. For the past decade, the tooling landscape for software engineers has been dominated by scriptable, interpreted languages. Python was the backbone of cloud infrastru…
articles.body: Originally published on tamiz.pro . The Performance-Reliability Nexus For the past decade, the tooling landscape for software engineers has been dominated by scriptable, interpreted languages. Python was the backbone of cloud infrastructure orchestration and data pipelines. Go provided the scaffolding for container runtimes and lightweight microservices. Node.js drove the build tools that glue the frontend world together. While these ecosystems are mature, they have hit a ceiling. As systems have grown in complexity—particularly in data engineering, CI/CD pipelines, and large-scale package management—the overhead of garbage collection (GC), dynamic typing, and high-level abstractions has become a bottleneck.

articles.title: Step-Up MFA Is the Wrong Response to Credential-Theft Tools in a Privileged Session
articles.excerpt: Most session-control products respond to a risky command the same way: pause, ask for another MFA prompt, continue if the user passes. For many commands that is reasonable. A destructive command in th…
articles.body: Most session-control products respond to a risky command the same way: pause, ask for another MFA prompt, continue if the user passes. For many commands that is reasonable. A destructive command in the wrong directory is usually a mistake by someone who is allowed to be there. A second factor confirms the person, and the person can explain. For credential-theft tooling it is the wrong control. The question is not "is this really you?". It is "why is a credential-dumping tool being used in a production session at all?". A valid second factor does not answer that. It confirms that the right person, or the right person's stolen session, is about to dump credentials.

articles.body: You exported a WhatsApp chat, imported it into Telegram, and the text arrived. Every photo, video and voice message turned into a line of text like <attached: IMG-20231104-WA0007.jpg> . The memories are gone and only placeholders remain. You did nothing wrong, and your export is fine. This is a known Telegram bug that has been open for over a year on Telegram's own tracker ( bugs.telegram.org/c/49513 ), with the same complaint in other bug threads , r/Telegram and Superuser. The text transfers and the media is silently skipped. This post explains why it happens, and how to import a WhatsApp chat into Telegram with the original dates and the media actually attached: photos, videos, voice messages, round video notes and stickers.

A huge problem with having so many tabs open at once is that it’s hard to keep track of what useful information a tab contains. For a long time, I used Stickies — the built-in sticky notes app on Mac — to write down important notes from these open tabs for my initial research. articles.title: Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way
articles.excerpt: A citizen science project is seeking volunteers to comb through NASA telescope data for telltale signs of the galaxy's hidden black holes.
articles.body: Astronomers estimate that our home galaxy, the Milky Way, has churned out more than 10 million black holes over its 13-billion-year history. Yet so far, they have found only 70. Now, a group of astronomers in the U.K. is trying to close that vast gap by enlisting the public. Their project, called Black Hole Hunters , is looking for volunteers with a computer and a few spare minutes to sift through troves of data gathered by a NASA space telescope. By flagging recognizable patterns that could point to a "missing" black hole , volunteers can help fast-track a search that would otherwise take years, the team says.

articles.title: The Pixel 11 Pro’s 120x zoom is ridiculous, but is it actually useful?
articles.excerpt: The Pixel 11 Pro's extreme zoom is surprisingly useful, but its AI-enhanced images come with some glaring caveats.
articles.body: Google has never been shy about pushing smartphone cameras to their limits. In fact, some might say, eking out the maximum using software instead of hardware is Google’s entire shtick with the Pixel lineup. With the Pixel 11 Pro , the company is taking things even further, quite literally, with 120x Pro Res zoom. That’s a step up from 100x on the Pixel 10 Pro and a ridiculous amount of magnification for a phone. Google claims its brighter telephoto camera can capture more detail from farther away – when combined with generative AI, of course. But just because a phone can zoom in that far doesn’t mean the results will be any good. My previous experience with such bold claims has often fallen flat. So, I was curious to see if Google could do any better.

articles.title: I’ve been a smart home user for 10 years, and the Apple HomeView looks like a game-changer
articles.excerpt: From intrusive ads to clunky software, the smart home landscape has a lot of room to improve. The HomeView could help.
articles.body: Smart displays are a category that, to me, have always felt like they’re on the cusp of being the next big thing for the smart home. I was excited when I first got my Nest Hub . The idea that I could control connected devices with a tap, without having to shout commands at a speaker or pull out my phone, was incredibly appealing. Want to turn off the lights? Just tap a button. Simple, practical. Fast forward to today, and it’s hard not to feel like the category has gone nowhere. Google’s Nest Hub displays are getting long in the tooth, while Amazon’s Echo Show lineup has become increasingly difficult to recommend when so much of the screen real estate is effectively used as a digital billboard.

articles.title: Before Dark Souls, FromSoftware’s Forgotten PS1 Horror Game Was a Haunting Exercise in Empathy
articles.excerpt: FromSoft’s Echo Night asks players to bring peace to the dead.
articles.body: To trace FromSoftware’s history is to uncover a lineage written in cold sweat. While the studio is celebrated today for unforgiving action RPGs like Dark Souls and Elden Ring , its DNA is deeply rooted in games that feel born of a fever dream. FromSoft’s darker legacy lives in games like Kuon , a masterclass in Japanese folklore and survival horror, and Shadow Tower , a claustrophobic dungeon crawler that turns every dark alcove into a deadly trap. Even Eternal Ring — not to be confused with its blockbuster sibling Elden Ring — radiates that signature, unsettling aura that makes exploring FromSoftware’s later worlds so intoxicating.

It’s not the flashiest in the lineup, and it’s not the least expensive, but if you want Moto’s latest at a reasonable price, one device should top your list.

articles.title: 10 best places to see the 2027 total solar eclipse in Spain
articles.excerpt: From the Costa del Sol to whitewashed mountain villages, here are 10 of the best places in southern Spain to experience the Aug. 2, 2027 total solar eclipse.
articles.body: Spain is one of the easiest places in the world to experience the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . The so-called "eclipse of the century" first makes landfall in Andalucía, where totality will last up to 4 minutes and 40 seconds during mid-morning, with the sun comfortably high at around 38-42 degrees above the horizon in the eastern sky. Excellent roads, plentiful accommodation and Málaga's international airport make this an obvious alternative to North Africa and the Middle East. However, choosing where to watch requires some thought.

articles.title: 'Let's all choose to make tomorrow better', Artemis II astronauts honored with Stephen Hawking Medal at Starmus
articles.excerpt: The Artemis II crew have joined an impressive list of honourees, including Buzz Aldrin, Jane Goodall and David Attenborough.
articles.body: TENERIFE, CANARY ISLANDS — The Artemis II astronauts may have traveled hundreds of thousands of miles away from Earth to the moon, but they made sure the rest of us didn't miss out on the adventure. Now, their efforts to bring the wonders of space exploration back down to Earth have earned them one of science communication's most prestigious honors: the Stephen Hawking Medal. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Victor Glover , alongside Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen , accepted the award on Saturday (Oct. 17), during the opening ceremony of the Starmus VIII festival. The honor recognizes all four crew members, including NASA astronaut Christina Koch , who wasn't in attendance.

articles.body: I got my hands on the Google Pixel 11 Pro XL when it launched globally in August, and I’ve spent quite a bit of time with it since. It’s not my daily driver, but I’ve used it enough to know what I love about it and, more importantly, where I wish Google had done things differently. If there’s one thing I’ve come to appreciate about Pixel phones over the years, it’s how Google gets so many of the little things right. From the design and software to how everything feels in everyday use, using a Pixel has a certain charm that’s hard to ignore. Of course, that doesn’t mean everything is perfect. Performance is still one area where I’d love to see Google step things up, especially when you look at what the competition has to offer.

Something where he’s telling you who he is with complete self awareness. I wanted the character's philosophy on life. To me, that’s the difference between a brilliant Charlie Brown quote and brilliant Charles Schulz quote, if that makes sense.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 17, 2016: Private Antares rocket returns to flight after catastrophic launch explosion
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, the Antares rocket now built by Northrop Grumman Space Systems returned to flight to come back from a catastrophic explosion. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 232 — The Lunar Dump
articles.excerpt: On Episode 232 of This Week In Space, Rod Pyle and Tariq Malik are joined by Chelsea Gohd to talk about the recent large data dump from the Artemis II mission.
articles.body: On Episode 232 of This Week In Space , Rod Pyle and Tariq Malik are joined by Chelsea Gohd, former writer for NASA/JPL and now with Space.com, to talk about the recent large data dump from the Artemis II mission. What was included? Why is this new data important? What observations were made, and what discoveries might result from them? What kind of annotations and notes did the astronauts include that make these observations uniquely valuable? And finally, we talk about Artemis III - what is the mission profile and what are the stakes for SpaceX and Blue Origin? Download or subscribe to this show at: https://twit.tv/shows/this-week-in-space .

articles.body: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes. But what happens when the rest of the internet won't play nice? In recent weeks, users of services like Meta's Muse, xAI's Grok, OpenAI's Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
